name: UniMate
description: [SIGGRAPH Asia 2026] UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
one_liner: A research AI model that can take motion from one creature, like a dog walking, and apply realistic movement to completely different skeletons — bipeds, birds, insects, even rigid objects — using one system instead of building a separate animator for each.
buyer: A game studio or animation house that needs to animate many different character types without hand-animating or retraining a separate model for each skeleton.
business_use_cases: An indie game studio quickly prototypes movement for a menagerie of creature types without hiring a dedicated animator per creature.
A VFX or ad studio generates quick animated motion previews for unusual rigs (mascots, robots) at pitch stage before committing to full animation work.
A research lab or university licenses tooling built on it for biomechanics or robotics motion research.

money_ideas.idea: A motion-design studio offers 'fast creature animation previews' as a paid pre-production add-on for game studios, built on top of this pipeline.

steal_this: This weekend, run the pretrained checkpoints against 3-4 unusual rigs from your own game or animation project and package the output as a quick concept-animation demo reel to pitch to a studio. Note: this requires real machine-learning expertise to productize, it isn't a plug-and-play tool.
